text:
maria: heads-up — after the kernel bump on eu-west1 (5.15 -> 5.19) the local-ssd health-checker started flapping nvme devices on a small set of nodes. devices get marked failed, then the node goes read-only, and gpu provisioning for batch jobs is blocked. :rotating_light:
ryan: can you paste the health-checker log?
maria: `[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] health-checker: nvme0n1: error count 5 -> marking failed
[2026-03-18T09:12:04Z] fs: remounting /var/lib/containers read-only
[2026-03-18T09:12:05Z] gpu-provisioner: failed to attach scratch volume -> evict`
lee_ops: is this limited to eu-west1 or hitting other regions?
olivia: we're seeing provisioning queue backups in eu-west1 only so far, ~8 nodes affected, fallback to reserved pool increased cost for live jobs.
maria: restarted the health-checker service on one node and the device came back but it flapped again after ~12m.
ryan: two hypotheses: 1) kernel NVMe timeout/firmware interaction increased transient error counts, 2) health-checker debounce threshold is too aggressive for 5.19.
janitor-bot: [alert] local-ssd-health-checker: node-gpu-012 marked device nvme0n1 failed (eu-west1)
lee_ops: quick mitigation: bump the health-checker error threshold and ignore single transient blk_reset errors. can we push a 10m disable on the pool while we patch?
maria: tried temporary kernel param tweak on test node: `echo 60 > /sys/module/nvme_core/parameters/io_timeout` — it reduced re-marks but didn't eliminate the flapping. logs still show periodic telemetry resets from the controller.
ryan: do we have the firmware build IDs? want to check known 5.19/firmware regressions. if firmware is flaky we should rollback kernel on affected hosts.
olivia: rolling back kernels will be disruptive to running workloads; what's the impact window and capacity hit if we drain 8 nodes in eu-west1?
lee_ops: estimate: draining 8 nodes reduces GPU capacity ~12% in eu-west1 for 2-4 hours, fallback spill to other regions + reserved capacity will add cost ~25% above baseline for that window.
maria: immediate plan: disable health-checker for the affected autoscaling group (1h), cordon the worst nodes, move critical jobs off them, and apply a health-checker debounce patch (PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/health-checker/pull/892).
ryan: +1. also open a firmware ticket with the OEM with logs attached. if the patch doesn't hold we do kernel rollback on a rolling subset.
janitor-bot: [action] Scheduled maintenance: disable-health-checker (eu-west1-pool-3) — start 2026-03-18T10:05Z, duration 1h.
olivia: assign oncall to watch provisioning queues and cost alerts during mitigation window — @ryan, you oncall?
ryan: I'm oncall for the hour, will watch the queue and tracer. set alert thresholds lower for provisioning latency.
maria: rollback plan queued as fallback. I'll coordinate the PR merge and restart sequence now. will post short postmortem after we confirm stability. :thumbsup:
lee_ops: once stable, add a robust debounce and a health-checker read-only hysteresis so a single controller reset doesn't trigger a full device fail. file the follow-up ticket in infra backlog.
maria: PR merged and rolling restart started at 2026-03-18T10:12Z. early signals: evictions dropped from 6/min -> 0-1/min, provisioning backlog shrinking. will keep mitigation for 1h then re-enable the stricter checks.
olivia: good, monitor cost dashboard for spillover — if spend delta > 20% abort and roll back nodes to previous kernel set.
maria: noted. postmortem + firmware ticket + debounce follow-up will be drafted. thanks team.
